title: Young children drown more easily because they cannot yet judge water or swim
summary: WHO says young children are at high drowning risk because they cannot yet judge danger well and often cannot swim, especially without an adult watching.
body: WHO's drowning fact sheet says young children are at particularly high risk because of an underdeveloped ability to assess risk and a lack of swimming and water safety skills. The risk rises when children meet water outside active adult supervision. A death-count card already records the sheet's global numbers, including the share among children under five, so those figures are not repeated here. This card is the reason the sheet gives for the age pattern. It is a global description, not a judgment of one child's character. Rescue breaths and the rest of a drowning response are on the first-aid cards.
